source.printedPageMapping: Printed pp.1–128 map to PDF pp.2–129; PDF1 and PDF130 are unprinted covers.

ownedTopics: equipment costs, package variants and prices
weapon proficiency, weapon weight/damage, general and missile hit-adjustment tables
hirelings, henchmen, time and distance procedures
spell-casting procedures and class-level spell-list table support

boundaryHandoffs.handling: Pixel-inspected as page boundaries; no duplicate regrade of p.33 two-class procedure or p.34 non-equipment units.

scope.productScopeNote: The current site snapshot is evidence of exposed owner/detail/search surfaces. No current-monster-catalogue feature exclusion is used to waive the PHB p.40 generic terminology or any other exposed rule facts.

method.pixelReview: Original PHB PDF images were rendered at 216 dpi; each source image was inspected separately, one image per result, with printed folio visible. Table-specific 288/360 dpi crops were also inspected separately. OCR/text extraction supported navigation only; source assertions derive from printed pixels.
method.siteJoin: Frozen 1,000-owner snapshot; each cited owner has rendered detail text and a captured public-search document where indicated. This records captured route/detail/search content, not live query ranking or source-chip navigation.
method.wholeBookLimit: This is a closed review of the delegated page cohort, not a complete PHB catalog or item-by-item verification of all source values.

pageCoverage.contentUnits: Contents for tables/charts and opening preface material.
Introduction/game advice, discretionary rules statement and referee-authority statement.
Character creation framing and four stated meanings of “level”.
Boundary page: dual-class/multiclass continuation; regraded elsewhere, not duplicated here.
Boundary/handoff: establishing characters, languages and other p.34 prose remain in prior PHB cohort.
Money, starting money, exchange/banking/loans/jewelers, equipment-selection, first half of cost table.
Cost table continuation, armor/shield rules and Armor Class Table, weapon-selection/proficiency introduction.
Weapon Proficiency Table and notes; Weight and Damage by Weapon Type with aliases and charge-damage notes.
Weapon Types/General Data/To Hit adjustments and Hurled Weapons/Missiles table with notes.
Hirelings, henchmen, time and distance procedures.
Generic “monster” definition, spell-casting exposition and cleric spell list.
Magic-user continuation, illusionist list and page-bottom illustration.

sourceAssertions.assertion: The contents and charts/tables list are navigational aids, not rules or procedures.
sourceAssertions.siteEvidence: The frozen snapshot contains no PHB table-of-contents page owner; no product claim follows because navigation/index feature coverage is outside this source-content cohort.

limits: No line-by-line transcription of the TOC/table index was made; its navigation-only kind was pixel-reviewed.

sourceAssertions.assertion: The preface discusses editorial framing and the intended role of the rulebooks; it does not present a bounded game procedure or lookup table.
sourceAssertions.siteEvidence: Excluded by content kind (preface/editorial matter), not because a site owner was counted as a pass.

limits: Editorial prose was not transcribed verbatim.

sourceAssertions.target: PHB source meaning represented in rules/search surfaces
sourceAssertions.assertion: The introductory text says rules are guidelines/suggested methods in many places and makes the campaign referee the final arbiter.

siteEvidence.negativeScope: No captured PHB Rules owner or public-search document in the complete 1,000-owner snapshot contains this adjudication statement; the analogous direct-attack DMG combat card is unrelated.

sourceAssertions.assertion: Challenge balance, cross-campaign compatibility, roleplaying advice and general encouragement occupy the rest of the introduction.
sourceAssertions.siteEvidence: General editorial/play advice, not a bounded mechanics/reference unit.

limits: The referee-authority statement is guidance, not a combat procedure; the audit records its absence without asserting every introductory paragraph is product scope.
P.7 source prose was classified by meaning; no full prose transcription.

sourceAssertions.assertion: A participant creates one or more personas; at campaign start the referee is advised to limit each participant to one. Abilities are generated randomly by dice; then race, class, alignment and name are chosen; languages follow race/class/alignment; starting gold buys equipment; class determines starting hit dice; every character begins at level 1.
sourceAssertions.evidenceDetail: The card paraphrases ability generation, race/class/alignment, languages, money/equipment and hit points. It does not state dice/random generation, persona/name, recommended one-at-start limit, class-determined hit die, or first-level start.

sourceAssertions.assertion: Printed p.8 uses “level” for character power, dungeon depth, spell difficulty, and monster threat.
sourceAssertions.siteEvidence: No captured rule owner/search text explains these four uses as a terminology note; related class/spell/monster records do not supply this four-way definition.

limits: This page does not prescribe a specific ability-score dice formula; it says abilities are generated by random dice. Detailed methods occur elsewhere.

sourceAssertions.assertion: Exchange ratios, relative coin size/weight and a typical 3% money-changing fee are stated.
sourceAssertions.evidenceDetail: Current card contains 1 gp = 20 sp = 200 cp = 2 ep; 1 pp = 5 gp; similar size/weight; typical 3% exchange.

sourceAssertions.assertion: Five class rows give starting-money ranges and dice: cleric 30–180 (3d6), fighter 50–200 (5d4), magic-user 20–80 (2d4), thief 20–120 (2d6), monk 5–20 (5d4), followed by the roll-and-total instruction.
sourceAssertions.siteEvidence: No current PHB Rules owner or the PHB equipment owners in the frozen snapshot represents the p.35 starting-money class table or dice instruction; `money-conversion` is only exchange.

sourceAssertions.assertion: The page gives a money-changer/banking procedure, no usual interest on deposits, collateral/reputation-based loans with typical 10% per month or 5% per week and lower rates around 1% per week for established borrowers; jewelers generally buy at 20% below actual value; local supply/demand distorts prices; shop around.
sourceAssertions.evidenceDetail: Only the 3% changer fee is stated by the money card; equipment-selection paraphrases seller availability/price variation but not supply-demand, loan terms, interest, collateral, or the jeweler purchase discount.

limits: The source financial service passage has prose procedures rather than a fixed table; no wording beyond the listed terms/rates was copied.

sourceAssertions.assertion: The source price table has 165 separately printed price rows across ten categories. Physical row count is distinct from item-owner count and selected price-field count.

siteEvidence.reconciliation: The Arrow owner stores a normal single price plus a separate dozen-price field, so physical price lines and priced owner records do not have a 1:1 count. Four PHB weapon-profile owners without a printed cost-table price are Bo Stick, Club, Quarterstaff, and Sling Stone. This count comparison is not a 165-row value/citation pass.

sourceAssertions.assertion: Source rows distinguish sale packages and variants, including normal arrows individually/by dozen, silver arrow individually, quarrel units, sling bullet packs, quiver capacities, one-week rations and vial contents; these units must not be collapsed to a per-item amount.
sourceAssertions.evidenceDetail: The Arrow card stores single and dozen prices separately; the data has separate sling-bullets-dozen and bolt/arrow-quiver owners. No complete 165-row physical-to-owner crosswalk was independently established in this cohort.

sourceAssertions.assertion: The current item records collectively expose only selected price/value fields; the source rows are not reproduced as one complete cost table.
sourceAssertions.siteEvidence: The frozen snapshot has 168 PHB equipment owners. Existing checked price rows are narrow citations; owner count and cards do not prove all row amounts, package labels, or category memberships.

limits: Source physical row counts are complete from the two pixel-reviewed printed pages. Exact current value and category joins were not manually closed for every one of 165 rows.
“gp-weight” in the weapon tables is weight/encumbrance, never a purchase-price row.

sourceAssertions.assertion: The PHB maps unarmored through plate/shield combinations across AC 10 to 2; shield alone is AC 9, and each +1 magical armor/shield lowers AC by 1 with a worked plate/shield example.
sourceAssertions.evidenceDetail: Current card reproduces base armor classes, shield-only, plate+shield, and magical +1-per-step rule, but not the complete row-by-row combination table/printed table surface.

sourceAssertions.assertion: Shield cover assumes the wearer can interpose it from the front; small/normal/large shield can protect against 1/2/up-to-3 melee attacks per round; attacks from right flank/rear nullify benefit.
sourceAssertions.evidenceDetail: Card includes interposition assumption, shield sizes/counts and flank/rear exception.

sourceAssertions.assertion: The source says magic armor negates encumbrance weight for movement.
sourceAssertions.siteEvidence: No PHB armor/equipment or Rules owner/search text in the frozen snapshot contains this movement-weight exception.

limits: Dexterity adjustment is referred to as a modifier here but its table is on p.12 and owned by the ability/race cohort.

sourceAssertions.assertion: Ten class rows supply initial proficient weapon count, non-proficiency penalty and additional proficiencies per levels above first.
sourceAssertions.evidenceDetail: The current card lists all ten source classes with the three numeric values.

sourceAssertions.assertion: Source notes explain that initial number permits choice among allowed weapon types, penalties apply to missile or melee attacks, proficiency with an ordinary weapon covers the same magical type, and level intervals are levels above 1st (illustrated with cleric acquisition at levels 1/5/9/13).
sourceAssertions.evidenceDetail: Card covers same-type magical proficiency, attack-roll penalty and column meanings; it does not include the permitted-choice examples or cleric progression example.

limits: P.36 begins this procedure and p.37 has its complete table/notes; both page segments are included.

sourceAssertions.target: equipment profile fields, rendered cards and search
sourceAssertions.assertion: Fifty physical weapon/ammunition rows list approximate gp-weight, damage against S/M and L, plus row notes/aliases.

siteEvidence.evidenceDetail: Selected item cards expose numeric weight and damage, but the field counts are below the 50 source-row denominator and some listed equipment is price-only. There is no single public 50-row table.

sourceAssertions.assertion: PHB Jo Stick row: 40 approximate gp-weight, 1–6 S/M and 1–4 L; the source-specific PHB/UA rows remain labeled separately rather than merged.
sourceAssertions.evidenceDetail: The public Jo Stick card keeps PHB p.37/p.38 and UA p.26/p.27 fields separate. PHB values match the inspected PHB rows. This is one row handoff, not whole-table verification.

sourceAssertions.assertion: The table contains ten row-level alias/variant notes and three distinct damage-qualification notes: italicized set-against-charge condition, one-asterisk mounted charge, and double-asterisk set-against-charge condition.
sourceAssertions.siteEvidence: Some cards have their numeric fields and narrow item details; the captured corpus was not found to contain the complete source table note/alias roster. Exact italic row membership was not fully rostered.

limits: Physical row denominator and note count are source-first; no inferred formula or reconstructed row values.
The exact membership of the p.37 italic typography condition is not independently rostered; marker meaning is legible and recorded.

sourceAssertions.target: equipment PHB p.38 field owners and public search
sourceAssertions.assertion: The hand-held table has 44 rows and gives dimensions, speed and AC-specific adjustments across nine target AC columns.

siteEvidence.evidenceDetail: Item records carry selected table values; only 21 PHB-book owners have these PHB p.38 field families, plus the UA Jo Stick owner with PHB fields. This is materially fewer than 44 rows.

sourceAssertions.target: PHB combat/rules searchable content and equipment details
sourceAssertions.assertion: The source specifies italicized dismounting, asterisk disarming on a needed AC 8 hit, double-asterisk one-handed bastard-sword treatment, and a general +2 to hit an opponent’s back/similarly unseen and +4 vs stunned/prone/motionless.
sourceAssertions.evidenceDetail: Ranseur has a p.38 disarm field and Bastard Sword carries the PHB one-handed rule; the PHB `Spetum` owner has no p.38 row fields. `flank-and-rear-attacks` (DMG p.70) overlaps the +2/+4 circumstances but adds shield/dexterity context and uses DMG source, so it is not a complete PHB p.38 association. No PHB card states the italic dismount condition.

sourceAssertions.assertion: Fifteen hurled/missile rows have rates, short/medium/long bands and short-range AC adjustments; one source note defines rate per tabletop turn/melee round and another applies −2 at medium and −5 at long range.
sourceAssertions.evidenceDetail: The shared rule card gives −2/−5 and short-range assumption; four PHB bow owners carry PHB p.38 fire rates/range bands. The other eleven physical rows are not represented with PHB p.38 row-level rate/range/AC vectors in PHB equipment fields.

limits: The p.38 italicized row roster was not fully transcribed; meaning is clear but exact marked-row coverage remains bounded uncertainty.
This table has an open-hand row without a corresponding PHB equipment owner; no inference that it should be priced.

sourceAssertions.assertion: Hirelings may be workers/servants/guards; their hiring depends on local availability, wage/bonus and some Charisma, the character locates them and sets local wages, terms may be hour/day/week/month/year, and ordinary hireling count is not Charisma-capped.
sourceAssertions.evidenceDetail: Card covers availability, offered terms, no ordinary hireling cap and variable employment periods; it omits the 11 named example occupations and the source’s locating/wage-setting detail.

sourceAssertions.assertion: Henchmen are distinct from ordinary hirelings; source includes Charisma attraction, compatible alignment, recruitment expense, upkeep/wage, a share of treasure, and reduced experience (about 50%, possibly less), with loyalty affected by remuneration, activity, treatment and conduct.
sourceAssertions.evidenceDetail: The p.39 henchman card captures upkeep, treasure, alignment and roughly half/lower XP; p.13 Charisma card separately covers maximum/loyalty modifiers. The p.39 recruitment process/costs and loyalty drivers are not all in the current henchman detail.

sourceAssertions.assertion: Dungeon turn=10 minutes; turn has ten 1-minute melee rounds and each round ten 6-second segments; outdoors time is in days with daylight movement/night rest, and elapsed campaign time controls upkeep and other activities.
sourceAssertions.evidenceDetail: The card accurately includes 10-minute/1-minute/6-second values and 10/10 subdivisions; it does not include outdoor day/night accounting or the longer time-cost examples.

sourceAssertions.assertion: Range notation uses 1 inch=10 yards outdoors and 10 feet indoors, with outdoor range conversion only; spell area stays at 1 inch=10 feet unless 1:10 or 1:20 figure scale is used; source gives actual bow/archery/slings/javelin range context, crossbow exception and leaves movement scale flexible.
sourceAssertions.evidenceDetail: Current rule card states basic conversions, no outdoor spell-area tripling, and existence of scaled-miniature exception; it omits the precise 1:10/1:20 conditions, practical range examples, crossbow visibility exception and flexible movement-scale procedure.

limits: `rules:charisma-henchmen` is a separate PHB p.13 owner: its content is credited only for the cross-page Charisma cap/loyalty facts, not as p.39 text.

sourceAssertions.assertion: The PHB defines “monster” as a generic term for creatures or people who may be encountered, not necessarily a hostile creature.
sourceAssertions.siteEvidence: No current PHB Rules owner for this definition and no captured searchable glossary/text owner; other monster usage does not reproduce this definition.

limits: The MM creature catalogue is outside the currently exposed feature, but this PHB terminology sentence is independently a rules-reference source unit and was not waived by that product boundary.

sourceAssertions.assertion: Spell casting may require verbal/somatic/material components; components and memorization/preparation are class dependent; magic-user/illusionist preparation uses spellbooks, takes about 15 minutes per spell level while rested/nourished, and each cast instance is expended although duplicates may be prepared.
sourceAssertions.evidenceDetail: Current cards cover component/interruption and expended-instance/duplicate rules. DMG p.40 study card gives the same 15-minute-per-level duration, but the PHB p.40 source association is absent; source page also gives selected-before-adventure and rest/nourishment prerequisites not fully represented in these cards.

sourceAssertions.target: rules:cleric-spell-acquisition + class/card/search representation of PHB fact
sourceAssertions.assertion: PHB p.40 says cleric/druid spells are bestowed by gods after prayer; levels 1–4 come through lesser servants, levels 5–7 only directly from deity; deity may refuse/replace requests based on conduct; some cleric and all druid spells need caster-supplied materials.
sourceAssertions.evidenceDetail: Current DMG-sourced card has different band labels (training 1–2, intermediaries 3–5, deity 6–7) from the PHB p.40 statement (lesser servants 1–4, deity 5–7); it does not preserve the PHB material-component exception. Treat this as an observed source-specific representation gap/possible cross-book disagreement, not an adjudicated rules contradiction; DMG original source was not re-read in this PHB cohort.

sourceAssertions.assertion: The source allows the DM to alter/add/delete spells, requires bulky or rare materials to be tracked/acquired, and directs class-specific exceptions before spell descriptions.
sourceAssertions.evidenceDetail: Individual components and interruption are described, but the blanket DM editing authority, bulky/rare-material handling, and class-specific transition instructions are not captured by these cards.

limits: This review compares PHB printed words with captured site surfaces and does not resolve how PHB and DMG rules should be harmonized.

sourceAssertions.target: spell owners, class/level fields and public-search docs
sourceAssertions.assertion: The printed list tables contain 414 class-level entries: 76 cleric, 78 druid, 194 magic-user and 66 illusionist, including one illusionist 7th-level pointer to a separate 1st-level magic-user list.
sourceAssertions.evidenceDetail: Current index owner counts per class/level match the visually counted source row counts; the captured site provides individual spell cards/search documents, not an ordered class-level table. Count parity does not establish exact names/order across all 414 occurrences.

limits: No complete name-by-name/order crosswalk was made for every table row; the source list structure is classified as partial, not passed from count parity.

excludedSourceKinds: general play-style advice except the bounded referee-authority assertion, which is recorded absent
notExcluded: money, equipment, armor, weapon, time/distance, spell procedures and reference-table content within public Rules/equipment/spell surfaces

limitations: Owner counts, search-document self-matches and field-key counts are not physical source-row completeness.
No live browser query, citation-panel opening, or source-image click-through was tested; snapshot.capture.sourceViewerOpened=false.
